elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The added sentence limits inspections to “not more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Existing §3.4 requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior” notice.
Existing §3.4 expressly requires prior written notice.

elements.element: Audits may be conducted only during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Existing §3.4 limits inspection to the Company's normal business hours.

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the inspection “shall be conducted ... by an independent auditor engaged by HDI.” Although the original grant to HDI's General Manager creates drafting tension, the new mandatory restriction expressly governs how the inspection is conducted.

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires the independent auditor to be bound by written confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: Existing §3.4 requires HDI to bear the fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection, without any cost-shifting right. That is at least as protective of Customer as allowing cost shifting only when underpayment exceeds 5%.

elements.element: The audit must not involve direct access to Customer's systems.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly states that the inspection “shall not include any direct access to the Company's systems.”

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The added once-in-any-12-month-period limitation meets the once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Existing §3.4 requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, exceeding the 15-day requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: Existing §3.4 requires HDI to bear its inspection fees without any underpayment-based exception, which is more protective of Customer than the fallback threshold.

result.reason: The operative language reaches both positions. It is not minimal because it also adds an unnecessary off-site-where-practicable requirement. Drafting quality and preservation suffer because the new audit sentence is placed after the Section 4 heading and creates tension with the existing statement that HDI's General Manager may inspect, while the new sentence requires the inspection to be conducted by an independent auditor.
